outcome.technical: plugins/audit/scripts/governance/_wave.py: overlap() and therefore select() now read both halves of what a task declares - its bare `files` entries (`_declared`, unchanged) and its `outputs` patterns graded by `_task_outputs.honoured`, the grading every other reader of the outputs half applies (`_config.declared_outputs` calls the same function), so a refused pattern covers nothing here either. New helpers _outputs, _entries, _segments, _segment_meets, _meets, _reaches, _named. A files entry is read as itself plus its subtree (`covers`), an outputs entry by `output_covers`; two entries meet when some path satisfies both, segment by segment, with `**` standing for any number of segments, a literal segment against a wildcard one asked of `_task_outputs.output_covers`, and two wildcard segments taken to meet (conservative: defer rather than admit two writers). The reported path is the literal the other entry reaches, else the entry with more segments, else both. files-vs-files behaviour unchanged (w1-w7c all pass). Module and select() docstrings now say both halves. tests/test__wave.py: new stage `wp` with wp1 (overlapping outputs, disjoint files -> deferred as overlap), wp2 (outputs pattern vs a files entry it covers, and a files directory vs a pattern under it), wp3 (second direction: patterns reaching no common path, and a refused pattern, stay one wave), wp4 (the overlap record names both tasks in id order, the covered literal, and a pattern reaching another task's lockfile is non-mergeable). PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md: the `_wave.py` tree line and section now say files and outputs. Mutations run in a separate process by monkeypatching (shared tree untouched): files-only _entries -> wp1/wp2/wp4 red 16/19; _segment_meets always True -> wp3 plus w1/w3b/w4/ws9/w5/w5c/wp4 red 11/19; ungraded outputs -> wp3 red 18/19.
